name: Rapid Wound Closure Epithelium
description: Enhances epithelial cell regeneration and migration speed, causing wounds to close at roughly 5 times the normal rate. A shallow cut that would take a week to heal closes in a day. A deep laceration that would take a month seals in a week. The modification does not heal internal injuries or regenerate tissue — it specifically accelerates the skin's ability to close wounds and form new epithelium. The result is rapid sealing of cuts, scrapes, and lacerations with reduced infection risk from shorter open-wound duration. The modification is the most practical medical geneware for daily life in the Gray Zone, where minor injuries are constant and access to medical care is limited. Helix Biosystems offers it as a bundle with clotting enhancement for comprehensive wound management.
source_organism: Ambystoma mexicanum (axolotl, epithelial regeneration), Tursiops truncatus (dolphin, rapid wound closure genes)
reversibility: Reversible with epithelial growth factor suppression
side_effects: Healed skin is slightly smoother and paler than surrounding tissue — scars are distinctive
Over-enthusiastic closure can trap debris in wounds if not cleaned first
Itching during rapid healing is intense
Rare: closure occurs around foreign objects embedded in wounds, requiring surgical removal
social_perception: Practical and unremarkable. Quick Seal is basic survival gear in the Gray Zone. Combined with Clotblood, it represents the minimum viable medical geneware package that street docs recommend for everyone.
story_hooks: A Quick Seal user's wound heals around a microdevice deliberately placed in the laceration — someone cut them to plant a tracker that their own body would seal in
A forensic examiner discovers that a wound pattern has been obscured by rapid healing — the victim's Quick Seal modification is destroying evidence of the weapon used
